prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1265; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the claimant reports a concussion with headache and dizziness shortly after the impact.

Entry 2: Confirmed with the insured that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active on the date of loss. Assigned the file for property damage and bodily injury review.

Entry 3: Contacted the other driver, who confirmed the sequence of events as first described. Police report on file lists the claimant as a passenger in the struck vehicle.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs taken at the scene. Rear damage to the vehicle is consistent with the reported impact speed and direction, and no prior damage was noted in the appraisal.

Entry 5: Two independent witnesses gave recorded statements that match the other driver's account and the police narrative. Nothing in their accounts conflicts with the physical evidence.

Entry 6: Claimant is now represented by counsel, who has requested that all communication go through the firm. Diverted further contact accordingly and noted the representation in the file.

Entry 7: Received medical records covering the emergency visit and follow-up. The concussion diagnosis fits the mechanism of the collision, and the records show no earlier treatment to the same area of the head or neck.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with symptoms easing over several weeks as the claimant improved and follow-up visits were reduced accordingly.

Entry 9: Claimant's counsel provided a supplemental statement adding minor details about seating position and the moment of impact. The core account is unchanged from the original report.

Entry 10: Reviewed the repair estimate against the damage pattern. The scope of repairs matches the described impact, and there is no indication the damage predates the policy's effective date.

Entry 11: Reserves updated to reflect the medical course and repair scope. File remains open pending final bills from the treating provider and counsel's demand package.
